_about: Resolve Political Monitor (Resolve Strategic, for The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age) one-off and occasional survey questions that do NOT channel into the auspol-tracker data model (voting intention, leader performance ratings, preferred prime minister, who-will-win expectations, party attributes and descriptors – the standing battery sits in polls.json and data/resolve-political-monitor.csv). Scope: the 48th parliament – waves of 2025-07-18 onward, the 17 Resolve waves on file in polls.json (latest: 2026-10-10; the 2025-08-16 and 2025-09-13 articles carried no topical questions). The Monitor publishes no questionnaire and no machine-readable one-off feed, so every wave's SMH/Age article (the url on the polls.json row) is the source: figures are the article's printed numbers verbatim (verbal figures like 'two in three' are noted in the entry's notes, never converted to numerals), question texts are our concise labels, and earlier readings cited only as trend references ride the notes rather than becoming entries of their own. Hand-curated like data/newspoll-one-offs.json; checked by .build/resolve-oneoffs.mjs – hand-edit the entries, never the generated field or key order.
_readme:
Emission rules:
- Scope: topical/occasional questions only. Excluded standing battery (channeled elsewhere): primary vote (incl. leadership-scenario primaries), leaders' good/poor performance, net likeability, preferred PM (two- and three-way), who-will-win, party attributes/descriptors, personal well-being index, vote firmness.
- One entry per question per wave. A question asked in several waves shares one id and becomes a series (most-important-issue, cgt-discount-removal, negative-gearing-restriction, trust-tax-increase, lower-house-prices, cost-of-living-blame, immigration-level, preferred-coalition-leader).
- Six ids are shared with the other houses' stores where the construct is the same question: immigration-level (SEC Newgate), gender-quotas-coalition, liberal-direction, economy-outlook-6m, preferred-coalition-leader (Essential), most-important-issue (News24).
- All figures are all-voters percentages printed in the wave's article; cells a wave never printed are null – never inferred from complements or trend sentences. Verbal-only figures ('two in three', 'almost a third', 'the third opposed', 'one in five') are covered by notes; the bar stays blank unless a numeral was also printed.
- Trend history printed in a later article (e.g. 'up from 48 per cent in December') lives in the entry's notes as printed context, not as a new wave entry.
- tables: the page's row shape – [label, ...values] with optional headers on crosstabbed reads; the first table is always the all-voters headline read. source repeats the wave article url for provenance.
